extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO EFS‑Web filers (including international/PCT and Hague design applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and technical requirements for filing patent and international design applications via USPTO (EFS‑Web and non‑electronic), handling of sequence listings/tables/reproductions, fees, filing receipts, return postcards, receipt/date stamping, and rules determining filing dates and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet count includes PDF sequence listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheet count for an EFS‑Web filed international application (PCT) containing both a PDF file and a text file sequence listing will be calculated to include the number of sheets of the PDF sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow‑on submissions of PDF files (including PDF sequence listings) may change the number of pages in the international application and therefore may affect the international filing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow‑on submissions timing and effect on international application
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence listing in an ASCII text file, as well as additional PDF files, may be submitted in one or more follow‑on submissions via EFS‑Web; such follow‑on submissions will form part of the international application (PCT) if filed on the same date on which the international application (PCT) was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sequence listing submitted after the international filing date in response to a requirement by the US ISA or IPEA under 37 CFR 1.821(h) and PCT Rule 13ter will not form part of the PCT international application as set forth in PCT Rule 13ter.1(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: No ASCII computer program listings under AI Annex F for PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for computer program listings in ASCII text file in international applications (PCT) under Annex F of the PCT Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web employs a web‑based approach and does not meet the AI Annex F 'wrapped, bundled and signed package' approach; consult Annex F of the PCT Administrative Instructions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables related to a sequence listing must be part of description and in PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables related to a sequence listing must be an integral part of the description of the international application (PCT), and must not be included in the sequence listing part or the drawing part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such tables will be taken into account when calculating the application sheet count (excess sheet fees may apply). When submitted via EFS‑Web, tables related to a sequence listing must be in a PDF file. Tables submitted in a text file will not be accepted as part of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct document description for DM/1 form
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants filing international design applications through the USPTO must present the application on the official Form DM/1 (or a form having the same form and content). Users should use the document description 'App for Intl Registration (DM/1 or equiv)' for a DM/1 form (or equivalent) submitted via EFS‑Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web will check for the presence of the document description when upload and validation are performed and will alert the user if the DM/1 form is not indicated as being attached. EFS‑Web will not block submission of a new international design application based on the missing document description, but the USPTO will not transmit the application to the International Bureau if applicant’s entitlement to file through the USPTO as office of indirect filing is not indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions requirement for international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions of industrial designs are required and may be submitted as drawings, photographs, or a combination, in black and white or color; they must satisfy technical requirements (resolution, minimum/maximum image size, border width) set by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproductions may be submitted through EFS‑Web as PDF or JPEG files. Each image file attached through the 'Attach Reproductions' section should contain only one view of the design. The 'Attach Reproductions' section will prompt assignment of design and view numbers to each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web file format and file size limits for reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS‑Web will not permit submission of any PDF or JPEG file via the 'Attach Reproductions' section that exceeds a file size of two megabytes. For PDF submissions via 'Attach Reproductions', EFS‑Web will not permit submission of any PDF file that is more than one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For JPEG submissions EFS‑Web provides warnings where requirements for image resolution and min/max dimensions have not been satisfied; EFS‑Web does not check color mode or border size for JPEG images. For PDF images, EFS‑Web does not check color mode, border size, resolution, or min/max dimensions other than certain minimum and maximum page size dimensions. It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure reproductions satisfy all applicable WIPO requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Reproductions vs Attach Documents other than Reproductions and fee warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may attach reproductions either via the 'Attach Reproductions' section or the 'Attach Documents other than Reproductions' section; attaching via the 'Attach Reproductions' section may help avoid incurring additional per page publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web will provide a warning about possible additional per page publication fees when reproductions are attached via the 'Attach Documents other than Reproductions' section. EFS‑Web will also warn if a new international design application does not contain an indication that at least one reproduction is attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes for national law requirements and document description
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application may be accompanied by annexes submitted for the purpose of complying with certain national law requirements (e.g., inventor’s oath/declaration where the US is designated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex forms specific to particular Contracting Parties are available on WIPO's website and should be attached to the EFS‑Web submission using the document description 'Annex(es) to the DM/1 or equivalent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal fee and payment deadlines for international design filings
rubrics_metrics.description: International design applications filed through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing are subject to payment of a transmittal fee. The USPTO will not transmit the international design application to the International Bureau if the transmittal fee has not been paid to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain international fees payable to WIPO may be paid through the USPTO provided they are paid no later than the date of payment of the transmittal fee; payments through the USPTO must be in U.S. dollars and may result in differences due to currency conversion. EFS‑Web will only permit payment of international fees payable to WIPO until 12 midnight Eastern Time of the date of payment of the transmittal fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Hague fee calculation guidance when using EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Calculate Fees' screen of EFS‑Web does not provide for individual selection of WIPO fees but provides for input of one lump sum in Swiss francs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should use the WIPO Hague Calculator to determine the total amount of fees required in Swiss francs, then copy and paste that amount into the 'International Fees Payable to WIPO (CHF)' field of the EFS‑Web Calculate Fees screen; EFS‑Web will calculate the U.S. dollar amount based on current exchange rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered users only may file follow‑on submissions in international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registered users may file follow‑on submissions via EFS‑Web in international design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an international design application was filed with the USPTO as an office of indirect filing, the USPTO will generally not forward communications to the International Bureau received after transmittal. Replies to invitations from the International Bureau must be filed directly with the IB to avoid abandonment or loss of rights under the treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of follow‑on submissions after transmittal but before WIPO publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow‑on submissions filed after transmittal to the International Bureau but prior to WIPO publication of the international design application designating the United States will generally be presumed to have been intended for consideration by the USPTO acting as an examining office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action by the Office on any such submission will generally be taken after receipt of the WIPO publication designating the United States. No follow‑on submission or fee payment is required from the applicant to initiate examination of an international design application that designates the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of reproductions under 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions amended pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121 may be submitted via EFS‑Web as either PDF or JPEG electronic files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such JPEG file must be attached using the 'Attach JPEG Reproductions' section of the 'Attach Documents' EFS‑Web screen. See other subsections for JPEG file size limits and limits on number of JPEG files per submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web Acknowledgement Receipt and application number assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, after successful submission an Acknowledgement Receipt is provided containing a time and date stamp, an application number, and a confirmation number; the Electronic Acknowledgement Receipt is the electronic equivalent of a postcard receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non‑electronic filings, a self‑addressed postcard will be provided with both the receipt date and an application number prior to returning it to the addressee; however, the application number on the postcard is a preliminary assignment and should not be relied upon as necessarily representing the application number assigned by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information that must be itemized on return postcard receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: The identifying data on the postcard should include inventor’s name(s); title of invention; number of pages of specification, claims, and sheet(s) of drawing(s); whether the inventor's oath or declaration is included; a list of any additional forms included; and amount and manner of paying the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A return postcard should itemize all components of the application; failure to itemize each component will mean the postcard will not serve as evidence that any unitemized component was received. Merely writing 'a complete application' will not suffice. The person receiving items at USPTO will check the listing against items submitted and initial any crossed‑off items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postcard postage and meter postmark requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure receipt of return postcards, users must either purchase already stamped postcards from USPS or affix postage stamps, or if a postage meter is used ensure that the meter postmark does not show the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any return receipt postcard containing a dated meter postmark may not be delivered by USPS to the address provided; postcards without sufficient postage or not acceptable to USPS may not be delivered and may be discarded. Applicants are solely responsible for proper postage and should check USPS requirements for acceptable card sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing receipt contents and controlling status
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP mails a filing receipt when the correspondence meets the minimum application requirements to receive a filing date; the filing receipt includes application number, filing date, confirmation number, and if available, the number of an art unit likely to examine the application, as well as other applicable information (continuing data, national stage data, foreign priority data, foreign filing license data, entity status, and anticipated publication date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing receipt represents the official assignment by the USPTO of a specific application number and confirmation number to the application. The application number on the filing receipt is controlling and may differ from a preliminary postcard application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation number usage and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The confirmation number is a four‑digit number assigned to each newly filed application and used in combination with the application number to verify accuracy of the application number on correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The confirmation number is included on the filing receipt, on cover sheets accompanying Office actions, and is available through the electronic filing system. Applicants are recommended to include the confirmation number (in addition to the application number) on all correspondence and when submitting a copy of the application for publication to avoid misidentification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of application number for Continued Prosecution Applications (CPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued prosecution application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design applications only) will be assigned the application number of the prior application for identification purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs are treated differently for filing date and identification as specified in 37 CFR 1.53(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules for nonprovisional, design, and provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received. The filing date for a design patent (except CPA) is the date the specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112, including at least one claim, and any required drawings are received. The filing date of a provisional application is the date the specification, with or without claims, is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced after the filing date. A provisional application filed before Dec 18, 2013 had to include any required drawings to be entitled to a filing date. Continuing applications must meet statutory conditions (35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) and § 1.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement and surcharge rules for inventor’s oath/declaration and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration, basic filing fee, and required search/examination fees may be filed later than the remaining application papers, but if so they must be accompanied by the required surcharge (if appropriate). For original applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, the filing of the inventor’s oath or declaration may be postponed until the date the issue fee is paid if an application data sheet is timely filed providing the required inventor information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The surcharge required for filing the inventor’s oath or declaration after the filing date must be paid on filing of the application or in response to a Notice to File Missing Parts. Failure to timely file required items may result in abandonment. For applications filed on or after Dec 18, 2013, the filing of at least one claim may be postponed until the expiration of the time period set in a Notice to File Missing Parts; claims and surcharge must be filed in response to that Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney docket number length and formatting limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney docket numbers must be limited to a maximum of 25 characters to prevent truncation; spaces, slashes, and hyphens will no longer be included in the entered docket number on the official filing receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'CASE' or 'NAVY-CASE' appears before the first character in the docket number, only the characters after CASE or NAVY‑CASE will be entered on the official filing receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑return of applications and fee refund rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications which are entitled to a filing date will not be returned to applicant even if requested (37 CFR 1.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change of purpose after payment of a fee (e.g., withdrawing the filing) will not entitle the party to a refund of such fee (37 CFR 1.26(a)); applicants must be careful not to file applications not intended to be filed (duplicates, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Date stamping rules for receipt of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO stamps papers and fees received through the mail (other than Priority Mail Express®) by facsimile, or via the electronic filing system with the date of their receipt in the Office (the "Office Date" stamp). Certain exceptions apply for Priority Mail Express®, facsimile, and electronic filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system is accorded a receipt date equal to the date in Eastern Time when the correspondence is received, regardless of local time or whether that date is a weekend or Federal holiday within the District of Columbia. When the last day for taking action or paying a fee falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, the action or fee is timely if done on the next succeeding business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile and Priority Mail Express® receipt dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence transmitted by facsimile will be stamped with the date on which the complete transmission is received in the Patent and Trademark Office unless that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, in which case the next succeeding non‑holiday day is used. New patent applications filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 (Priority Mail Express®) will be stamped with the date of deposit as Priority Mail Express® with USPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If deposited in Priority Mail Express® on a Saturday and USPS gives a Saturday deposit date, the Office will accord and stamp the correspondence with that Saturday date (37 CFR 1.6(a)(2)).
